<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s).

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 222293f60a7fff2779269b20bb4e5ce28a34c935`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 38 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 222293f60a7fff2779269b20bb4e5ce28a34c935` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f7b034e9686d927fbe023993afafb2274ed488b6` — the merge of head `fdc2dc05fc4c8029dad8cdc1c2f9b9e2c7d9cfe1` into base `222293f60a7fff2779269b20bb4e5ce28a34c935`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f7b034e9686d927fbe023993afafb2274ed488b6 && git checkout f7b034e9686d927fbe023993afafb2274ed488b6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 222293f60a7fff2779269b20bb4e5ce28a34c935 fdc2dc05fc4c8029dad8cdc1c2f9b9e2c7d9cfe1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 222293f60a7fff2779269b20bb4e5ce28a34c935 && git merge --no-ff fdc2dc05fc4c8029dad8cdc1c2f9b9e2c7d9cfe1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 222293f60a7fff2779269b20bb4e5ce28a34c935
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 222293f60a7fff2779269b20bb4e5ce28a34c935` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

`domain:spec` seat 4 (#18917) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_0121ooBYRmS8ziFXm9ai5YHm` · claim `6172782630` on #23505 · reviewed head `fdc2dc05fc4c8029dad8cdc1c2f9b9e2c7d9cfe1` · 2026-10-14T17:55Z

**Verdict: ACCEPT.** Not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 23522`): 5 files, +271 / −34.

1. **Shape.**
   - Draft PR. Its first line is `Fixes #23505`, and `Clause-②: no` sits at line start.
   - The changeset `.changeset/23505-extension-refusal-409.md` is `@objectstack/objectql` `patch` and carries FROM / TO / Unchanged plus a migration note for anyone matching the old text.
   - The ADR-0087 gate reads it as non-breaking. The request is refused in exactly the same cases as before; only the answer changes.
2. **The seat's decision against the diff.**
   - The fix is at the producer alone. `PackageUninstallExtendedError` (unexported, the registry's house shape) carries `code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT'`, `status: 409` and `httpStatus: 409`. It reuses a standard catalog member and mints no code.
   - The message leads with the way out and names every extended object (five, then a count) with its extenders.
   - `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` is untouched; PR #23504 holds `deletePackage` steps 1–4. The door answers the thrown status as is.
   - The refusal predicate and its iteration order are unchanged.
   - Caller census:
     - `deletePackage` step 3 and the door with no persisted half: `500` → `409`.
     - `deletePackage` step 6, the door's safety net, and cloud-connection's install-local withdrawal read `err.message` only, so only their log text changes.
     - `ObjectQL.removePackage` passes `force` and never asks.
3. **Gates and evidence.**
   - Head check-runs: 34 success, 6 skipped (the full-battery or opt-in set), 0 failures. `mergeable_state` is `clean`.
   - The re-pinned real-stack pin passes 5/5, every nothing-changes assertion kept, plus a prescription assertion and a door-level control.
   - Ablation: renaming `code`/`status` turned the re-pinned case red on exactly `{ status: 409, code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT' }` → `{ status: 500, code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR' }`. The `dist` marker was proven present, then absent after the restore.
   - Local reconciliation: 68 derived, 67 run, 1 NOT MEASURED (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, whole-tree; CI reads it).
   - `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` and `check:error-status-conformance` pass.
4. **Accepted deviations.**
   - The message names every extended object, within the seat's "names the object(s)" decision. The order pin now reads the structured refusal.
   - A one-off probe was deleted.
   - The objectql full suite was read at `a9a88b1e34`; the merge brought no objectql source.
5. **Out-of-scope dispositions.**
   - Two code comments still say the door answers `500`:
     - `protocol.ts`'s `deletePackage` step-3 comment, in PR #23504's region;
     - `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`'s DELETE arm.
     Both are comment-only, recorded in Acceptance notes, `carrier:` none.
   - `protocol.package-delete-refusal.test.ts` builds its fake refusal with the old sentence. It pins pass-through identity, so it stays valid.
6. **Landing clauses.**
   - (a) Every check green or skipped by design: met.
   - (b) `mergeable_state` clean at enqueue: met.
   - No contract review is owed. No accept set and no public key moves; only a refused request's answer changes from a server-fault `500` to the standard `409`.
